overview: Both are forms of genetic drift causing a sudden loss of genetic diversity, but they differ in how the small population arises.
genZNote: Founder effect: a tiny group breaks away and starts fresh elsewhere. Bottleneck effect: a disaster wipes out most of an existing population, leaving a random few.

aspects.label: Cause
aspects.valueA: A small group of individuals separates from a larger population to colonise a new area.
aspects.valueB: A sudden environmental event (disaster, disease, hunting) drastically reduces an existing population's size.

aspects.label: Population History
aspects.valueA: A brand-new population is established from a small founding group.
aspects.valueB: The same original population survives, but with drastically reduced numbers and diversity.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A few individuals colonising a remote island and founding a new isolated population.
aspects.valueB: Cheetah populations today show low genetic diversity due to a past near-extinction bottleneck event.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Cheetahs are a famous real-world bottleneck effect example, showing dramatically reduced genetic diversity from a past population crash.
overlay.memoryTrick: Founder effect = new colony started small. Bottleneck effect = existing population crashed down small.
overlay.commonMisconception: Both effects reduce genetic diversity through random chance, not natural selection — that's exactly why they're classified under genetic drift, not adaptation.
